lesson: Today we work on one thing, verbs. A verb is an action word. It tells you what someone or something does. The lesson is simple. Strong verbs do more work than describing words, so lean on them. Look at three spots. Where you stepped out of them uses stepped. So you see the motion, not just the boots. The reaching, the carrying, the bending to the work stacks three action words in a row. The cold floor finds your feet. The kettle wants its match. Gives the floor and the kettle their own verbs, finds and wants. This works because a verb makes you picture a thing moving. Your mind follows the action. That holds your attention better than a pile of adjectives. Try this. Take a line you wrote, cut one describing word, and put a specific action word in its place. The second time, listen for how all those small actions push toward one last command. So up.
